posts.body:
Are there any database editing tools for RPG Maker 2003 similar to the
MV/MZ Database Cleanup Tool
where I can move variables and items around without having to edit every other event and command that references them?

posts.author: DeeCompose_Bady
posts.body:
ANSWER FROM SOMEONE NOT VERY EXPERIENCED!
RPG Maker 2003 (as well as 2000) uses an older project file format that is less accessible to external scripts than the MV/MZ versions.
Data Format: RM2K3's event, map, and database data is stored in binary files (.LDB and .MAP) - (If I remember correctly). It's much harder for an external tool to parse these files to find all the ID references (which are stored as raw numbers) and rewrite them without corrupting the project.
The Risk: A tool that attempted this would have to be perfect, as a single byte rewrite error could corrupt the entire Event or even the project. Because of this high risk and technical complexity, the community never developed a complete "database wipe" tool for RM2K3 (Again: If I remember correctly).
---
Some alternatives would be...
Advance Planning: Best practice is to leave "holes" (empty spaces) between blocks of variables and items in the Database so that you can insert new items/variables later without messing up existing IDs (I don't know if it would work very well).
(I googled this part) Limited Search Tools: Using RM2K3's project editing tools (such as EasyRPG Editor or RPG Maker 2003 Event Patch) can help you quickly find where a specific variable or item is being used, making manual fixes faster. However, they won't automatically change the ID for you.
